newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks fall in morning after Wall St drop.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks fall in morning after Wall St drop.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks took a hit in Wednesday morning trade after an overnight decline in the Dow industrials prompted jitters among local investors, brokers said.
The Hang Seng index was down 77.60 points at 13,378.66. Turnover was HK$1.89 billion after the first 50 minutes of trade.
"I think it is just following the U.S. market," said Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities. He said the Hang Seng should find support at 13,300 points in the short-term.
The Dow industrials fell 79.01 points on Tuesday to 6,442.69, their biggest point decline since July.
"If the market cannot hold 13,300 it might have more downside. It might test 13,000," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
He said the 10-day moving average on the Hang Seng index was in the 13,300 point area.
"So far this rally (since the end of October) the index has not dipped below the 10-day moving average. If it cannot hold, it might signal a correction," said Tam.
He said that low turnover in the market, compared with last week's busy sessions, was a sign that some investors were awaiting a correction.
He added that a rise in H-shares may also be signalling "the end of the (upside) cycle for the short-term".
The H-share index was up 7.65 points at 842.46.

Shares in China Resources Enterprise rose HK$1.45 to HK$14.40 after the company said it agreed to buy a 10 percent stake in container terminal operator HIT Investments from its parent China Resources (Holdings) Co (CRH) for HK$3.5 billion.

It said it would pay HK$2.25 billion in cash and issue 111.11 million new shares at HK$11.25 per share to CRH. CRH has agreed to place 90.90 million existing China Resources Enterprise shares at HK$11.25 per share to private investors.
Chung Hwa Development shares rose HK$0.10 to HK$1.68. The company said it had raised about US$7.5 million from the U.S. listing of its Leading Edge Packaging Inc subsidiary.
Shares in Wheelock fell HK$0.20 to HK$21.60. The company is due to release its interim results on Wednesday.
Among the major blue chips, HSBC Holdings was down HK$0.50 at HK$161.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.75 to HK$96.50. Hutchison shed HK$0.75 to HK$59.25 and Swire was off HK$0.50 at HK$73.50.
